1. Personal Value Assessment:
- y has highest value ($74) and I have top priority there
- x is second-highest value ($63)
- z has moderate value ($58)
- w has lowest value ($49)

- This suggests y will be highly competitive
- My top priority at y is advantageous
- However, everyone knowing this might make y harder to secure
- x might be a strategic "safer" alternative with less competition

- If everyone ranks y first, competition increases
- A slightly contrarian approach of ranking x first might improve my chances
- I still want y high in my ranking to keep that option open

- Prioritize x to potentially reduce competition
- Keep y as a strong second choice
- Maintain z and w as fallback options
